# incident_access_grant (Resource)

Manage access grants: the privileges each access group gives its members across the whole account.

An access group holds one grant on the organization, so manage at most one `incident_access_grant` for each group. Creating a grant for a group sets that group's privileges, and adopts the grant the group already has.

You can manage the grants of the `admin` and `standard` base groups, but not of `owner`. A base group always keeps some privileges, so destroying the grant of a base group leaves its privileges as they are and only stops Terraform managing them.

Use the `incident_access_privileges` data source to see which privilege names you can grant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "incident_access_group" "responders" {
  name = "Incident responders"
}

# An access grant gives privileges to an access group across the whole organization.
resource "incident_access_grant" "responders" {
  principal = {
    type = "access_group"
    id   = incident_access_group.responders.id
  }
  resource = {
    type = "organization"
  }
  privileges = [
    "incidents.manage",
  ]
}

# You can also manage what the admin and standard base groups can do. Destroying one of
# these grants leaves the group's privileges as they are.
data "incident_access_group" "standard" {
  slug = "standard"
}

resource "incident_access_grant" "standard" {
  principal = {
    type = "access_group"
    id   = data.incident_access_group.standard.id
  }
  resource = {
    type = "organization"
  }
  privileges = [
    "incidents.manage",
    "schedule_overrides.manage",
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `principal` (Attributes) Who this grant gives privileges to. Changing it replaces the grant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--principal))
- `privileges` (Set of String) Names of the privileges this grant gives, stored and returned as sent. Unknown names return 422. A grant must give at least one privilege.
- `resource` (Attributes) What this grant gives privileges on. Changing it replaces the grant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource))

### Optional

- `unlock_in_dashboard` (Boolean) Whether to leave this resource unlocked in the incident.io dashboard, so people can edit it there. Defaults to `false`: Terraform claims what it manages, and a claimed resource cannot be edited in the dashboard. Set it to `true` to leave the resource unclaimed — pair that with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [...] }` naming the attributes people edit, or the next apply reverts them. Setting it on a resource Terraform already claimed hands that resource back, and someone disconnecting one in the dashboard shows as no change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this access grant. It does not change when the grant's privileges change.

<a id="nestedatt--principal"></a>
### Nested Schema for `principal`

Required:

- `id` (String) The principal's ID
- `type` (String) The kind of principal. Only access groups can hold grants today.


<a id="nestedatt--resource"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource`

Required:

- `type` (String) The kind of resource. organization means the whole organization.

## Import

Import is supported using an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) or the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import):

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
#!/bin/bash

# Import an access grant using its ID
# Replace the ID with a real ID from your incident.io organization
terraform import incident_access_grant.example 01ABC123DEF456GHI789JKL
```
